segments.speaker: Matt Rebar
segments.text: Brad and Harry's cheese curds have been at the Iowa State Fair since somewhere in the mid to early '90s.

segments.speaker: Chris Benderev
segments.text: Matt Rebar runs three cheese curd stands and one poutine stand here at the Iowa fair. And the way they operate has been refined over decades. And the biggest difference I noticed from Jamie and Jennifer's Biscuit Bar? Simplicity, all emanating from this fact.

segments.speaker: Matt Rebar
segments.text: We have one item. We have one item. It costs one amount. We know they're in line for cheese curds. We know what the change is. We can see in their wallet and know what bill they're going to grab, and we can already have the change ready by the time that transaction happens.

segments.speaker: Chris Benderev
segments.text: Biscuit Bar, by contrast, has 11 food items and 16 beverage choices, many with a bunch of different customizations.

segments.speaker: Matt Rebar
segments.text: It's volume. That's what we're after, is the volume. Quality, but volume.

segments.speaker: Chris Benderev
segments.text: Inside his trailer, it's tightly packed with employees in a smaller space than Biscuit Bar. But somehow, it's more orderly.

segments.speaker: Matt Rebar
segments.text: But as far as workstations and positions in here, that's another thing. Everybody in there has one job, and they are within one foot of what they need to do. They don't have to take two steps to do anything in there.

segments.speaker: Chris Benderev
segments.text: Really?

segments.speaker: Matt Rebar
segments.text: We have enough people where, if you needed to take two steps, we're going to put another person in there to do that for you, just to be efficient as much as possible.

segments.speaker: Chris Benderev
segments.text: The trailer was custom-built, so every step of making the food is laid out in perfectly sequential cheese curd assembly stations. Over at the Biscuit Bar, employees make complicated coffee drinks, smoothies, and pour fountain drinks. At Matt's cheese curd stands, his employees don't make drinks at all. Matt sees that as inefficient. Instead--

segments.speaker: Matt Rebar
segments.text: We've got a self-serve pop. Pop takes a lot of time, so if we can hand them a cup, they can go take their time, fill their ice as much as they want or as little as they want.

segments.text: One last note about the simplicity of Matt's cheese curd stands-- paper towels. People need them constantly in a kitchen, and Matt has positioned a roll that hangs horizontally from a bungee cord above the workers. They can grab and tear them off effortlessly without taking up any space. Meanwhile, back at Biscuit Bar--

segments.text: I didn't appreciate at first just how much Jamie sees opening a business at the fair as being like a trip to the casino. segments.text: It was just a wish. He was going to put his money down on the table, roll the dice, and hope for the best.
